tests.title: System info advertises LLM control-plane kinds only when enabled
tests.description: Reuses handler coverage for enabled and disabled `/api/v1/system/info` payloads. Estimated implementation difficulty: none; already covered.
preconditions: System handler can be constructed with `cfg.LLM.Enabled=true` and `cfg.LLM.Enabled=false`.
steps: Request system info with LLM disabled.
Request system info with LLM enabled.
Inspect advertised capabilities and request/status/result/read-model kind maps.
tests.expected_result: LLM capabilities and canonical kind families are present only in the enabled payload and absent in the disabled payload.
data_requirements: Stable handler config with deterministic `LLM.Enabled` values.
determinism_notes: Pure handler-level contract test; no network or relay dependency.

tests.title: LLM route create reactor emits correlated 7971 result for a signed 5971 request
tests.description: Reactor-level handler contract test that delivers a signed route-create event and inspects the published correlated terminal result. This proves request/result correlation and persistence on the Bahia side, but not requester-side relay acceptance semantics. Estimated implementation difficulty: medium.
preconditions: A reactor instance can be configured with an authorized requester and capture publisher.
A signer-generated 5971 request event can be produced deterministically in test.
steps: Publish a signed kind 5971 route-create request with valid content.
Handle the event through the reactor.
Inspect the published terminal reply event and decode its payload.
tests.expected_result: The reactor emits a signed kind 7971 result tagged back to the original request event and requester with `status=success` and a created `route_id`.
data_requirements: Stable route payload fixture with route name and gateway config.
Deterministic request pubkey and signed event id.
determinism_notes: Keep the test fully in-process; inject the signed request event directly rather than using live relays.
Assert reply tags include `e` and `p` correlation plus created `route` identifiers.
This test does not prove requester-side relay acceptance semantics.

tests.title: LLM registry MCP route-create tool persists route metadata
tests.description: Existing MCP test proves route creation persists a route and returns registry metadata, but it does not prove the signer-first 5971/7971 wire contract. Estimated implementation difficulty: none; keep as supporting coverage.
preconditions: MCP server is initialized with in-memory LLM route repository.
steps: Call `bahia_llm_create_route` with valid route payload.
Inspect returned `route_id` and registry kind.
Verify the route was persisted in the fake repository.
tests.expected_result: Route creation succeeds and persists state through the registry service.
data_requirements: Stable route name and gateway config fixture.
determinism_notes: Useful supporting evidence only; canonical Nostr request/result correlation is covered by LLMRD-T-002.

tests.title: LLM release register reactor emits correlated 7972 result for a signed 5972 request
tests.description: Reactor-level handler contract test for signed release registration and correlated terminal result emission. This proves route-scoped result correlation on the Bahia side, but not requester-side relay acceptance semantics. Estimated implementation difficulty: medium.
preconditions: A valid LLM route exists in the in-memory registry.
A reactor instance can be configured with an authorized requester and capture publisher.
steps: Publish a signed kind 5972 release-register request scoped to an existing route.
Handle the event through the reactor.
Inspect the published kind 7972 terminal result and decode its content.
tests.expected_result: The reactor resolves the request with a correlated kind 7972 result containing `route_id`, `release_id`, and `status=success`.
data_requirements: Stable route id and release payload fixture.
Deterministic request pubkey and signed event id.
determinism_notes: No live relay dependency; inject signed request event directly and assert `e`/`p` reply tags.
This test does not prove requester-side relay acceptance semantics.

tests.title: LLM registry MCP release-register tool persists release metadata
tests.description: Existing MCP test proves release persistence and returned ids, but not the signer-first 5972/7972 wire contract. Estimated implementation difficulty: none; keep as supporting coverage.
preconditions: MCP server is initialized with in-memory route and release repositories.
steps: Create a route.
Call `bahia_llm_register_release` for that route.
Verify the returned `release_id` was persisted in the fake repository.
tests.expected_result: Release registration succeeds and stores a release associated with the route.
data_requirements: Stable route id, version, and model reference fixture.
determinism_notes: Supporting persistence proof only; canonical Nostr request/result coverage belongs in LLMRD-T-004.

tests.title: LLM deploy request publisher emits explicit route/environment/release tags and fails on zero accept
tests.description: Extend command publisher tests to cover deploy, not just rollback, and assert explicit `route`, `environment`, and `release` tags plus zero-accept failure behavior. Estimated implementation difficulty: low.
preconditions: Command publisher can be constructed with a capture publisher and signer.
steps: Publish a valid deploy command with one accepted relay.
Inspect emitted request kind, signature, content, and tags.
Repeat with zero accepted relays.
tests.expected_result: Successful publish emits signed kind 5973 with explicit route/environment/release tags; zero-accept publish returns a local error and no false success receipt.
data_requirements: Stable route, environment, and release UUID fixtures.
determinism_notes: Pure publisher test; no live relay required.
Current suite already covers the zero-accept branch and needs the positive deploy-tag assertion added.

tests.title: Accepted deploy request emits initial correlated 6973 processing status
tests.description: Add a reactor test that proves the first reply to an accepted deploy request is a processing status, not terminal success. Estimated implementation difficulty: medium.
preconditions: A valid route, release, and environment exist.
An authorized requester can publish a signed deploy request.
steps: Deliver a signed kind 5973 deploy request to the reactor.
Inspect the first published correlated reply event.
Decode reply tags and content.
tests.expected_result: The first correlated reply is kind 6973 with `status=processing` and step `accepted`; it is not a terminal success result.
data_requirements: Stable route, release, environment, and requester fixtures.
determinism_notes: Inspect reply ordering directly from the in-process capture publisher.
Assert `e`, `p`, `route`, `environment`, and `release` correlation tags.

tests.title: MCP deploy tool returns canonical request/status/result metadata
tests.description: Existing MCP test verifies deploy tool payload shaping and returned canonical kind metadata. Estimated implementation difficulty: none; keep as supporting coverage.
preconditions: MCP server is initialized with capture LLM command publisher.
steps: Call `bahia_llm_deploy` with route, environment, release, and requester inputs.
Inspect returned request kind and event id.
Verify captured deploy command fields.
tests.expected_result: The MCP tool returns canonical deploy kind metadata and forwards the expected route/environment/release/requester values.
data_requirements: Stable route, environment, release, and requester values.
determinism_notes: Useful API-layer proof only; async acceptance semantics are covered by LLMRD-T-006 and LLMRD-T-007.

tests.title: LLM approval and rejection requests validate decision values and publish correlated 7973 results
tests.description: Add reactor coverage for valid approve/reject requests and invalid decisions. Estimated implementation difficulty: medium.
preconditions: A pending protected-environment LLM deployment intent exists.
An authorized requester can publish signed kind 5974 requests.
steps: Deliver an approve request for the pending intent.
Deliver a reject request for a fresh pending intent.
Deliver an invalid decision request.
Inspect terminal reply events and resulting intent state.
tests.expected_result: Approve and reject requests publish correlated kind 7973 results; invalid decisions fail validation without mutating state.
data_requirements: Stable pending intent fixtures for approve and reject cases.
Deterministic request pubkey and signed event ids.
determinism_notes: Keep approve, reject, and invalid-decision cases isolated so state mutations remain explicit.

tests.title: Rejected LLM intent is repaired out of desired route state
tests.description: Add registry coverage that rejection repair clears the rejected intent from desired route-state selection. Estimated implementation difficulty: medium.
preconditions: The registry service can be constructed with fake route, intent, run, observation, and state repositories.
A pending protected-environment intent is present in desired state.
steps: Create a desired-state intent for a protected environment.
Apply rejection through the registry service path used by the reactor.
Fetch route state after rejection repair.
tests.expected_result: Desired route state no longer points at the rejected intent after rejection repair completes.
data_requirements: Stable route, release, environment, and intent UUID fixtures.
determinism_notes: No relay dependency; assert state repository contents directly after rejection repair.

tests.title: MCP approval and rejection tools shape canonical request metadata
tests.description: Existing MCP coverage proves approve/reject command shaping and returned decision metadata, but not backend mutation or rejection repair. Estimated implementation difficulty: none; keep as supporting coverage.
preconditions: MCP server is initialized with capture LLM command publisher.
steps: Call `bahia_llm_approve_deployment`.
Call `bahia_llm_reject_deployment`.
Inspect returned decision metadata.
tests.expected_result: Approve and reject tools forward the correct intent id and decision strings through the command publisher boundary.
data_requirements: Stable pending intent UUID.
determinism_notes: Supporting request-shaping proof only; stateful approval behavior is covered by LLMRD-T-009 and LLMRD-T-010.

tests.title: Successful provisioning run emits staged 6973 progress and terminal 7973 completion
tests.description: Add coordinator coverage for the accepted-intent success path, including responder callbacks for progress and completion. Estimated implementation difficulty: high.
preconditions: A queued run exists for an accepted LLM deployment intent.
Fake placement, provisioner, gateway, registry, run repository, and responder dependencies are available.
steps: Invoke `ProcessOnce` for a queued successful run.
Capture responder status and result callbacks in order.
Inspect final run status and recorded observation/state.
tests.expected_result: The coordinator emits meaningful progress stages such as placement, provisioning, gate evaluation, gateway sync, and observation recording, then publishes a terminal completion result and marks the run succeeded.
data_requirements: Stable route, release, environment, intent, run, worker, and gateway-ref fixtures.
Deterministic successful backend observation and gateway observation payloads.
determinism_notes: Exercise `ProcessOnce` directly instead of ticker-based `Run` to avoid timer-driven tests.
Assert callback order deterministically from the capture responder.

tests.title: Provisioning failure emits terminal error result and leaves run failed
tests.description: Add coordinator failure-path coverage for provisioning, promotion-gate, or gateway-sync errors. Estimated implementation difficulty: high.
preconditions: A queued run exists for an accepted LLM deployment intent.
Fake dependencies can force provisioner, promotion gate, or gateway failures.
steps: Invoke `ProcessOnce` for a queued run whose provisioner or gateway path fails.
Capture responder callbacks.
Inspect final run status and recorded metadata.
tests.expected_result: The coordinator emits progress up to failure, publishes a terminal error result, records failure metadata, and marks the run failed instead of succeeded.
fixtures: fake failing provisioner or gateway manager
data_requirements: Stable queued intent/run fixtures and deterministic injected failure reason.
determinism_notes: Drive failures directly through fake dependencies; avoid sleeps or external runtime dependencies.

tests.title: Projector republishes authoritative LLM route and route-state read models
tests.description: Existing projector tests prove republished `31964` and `31965` events are signed and carry route/state tags from authoritative state. Estimated implementation difficulty: none.
preconditions: Fake projection source contains authoritative route, state, release, intent, and run data.
steps: Run snapshot republish with LLM projection source enabled.
Inspect emitted route registry and route-state projection events.
tests.expected_result: Signed `31964` and `31965` projection events are published with the expected route, environment, release, intent, run, and gateway-status tags.
data_requirements: Stable route, environment, release, intent, and run UUID fixtures.
determinism_notes: Projection events are captured synchronously and signature-checked locally.

tests.title: Registry and reconciler propagate observed backend and gateway state into LLM route state
tests.description: Existing registry and reconciler tests prove desired state becomes in-sync after observation and that reconcile observations carry backend/gateway state. Estimated implementation difficulty: none.
preconditions: Fake registry repositories and reconcile fixtures are available.
steps: Create an LLM deployment intent and inspect desired route state.
Record an observation and re-read route state.
Construct a reconcile observation from backend and gateway inputs.
tests.expected_result: Desired-vs-observed route state becomes in-sync after observation, and backend/gateway fields are preserved through reconcile observation shaping.
data_requirements: Stable route, release, environment, run, backend, and gateway observation fixtures.
determinism_notes: Pure in-process tests with deterministic fake repositories and observation inputs.

tests.title: Browser control-plane store bootstraps and applies Bahia-authored LLM read models and activity events
tests.description: Existing browser-store tests cover EOSE-aware bootstrap, live subscription bridging, and valid LLM route/state/activity event application. Estimated implementation difficulty: none.
preconditions: System info advertises a Bahia service pubkey and browser relay.
Shared Nostr client is mocked.
steps: Bootstrap the shared control-plane store.
Inject Bahia-authored route, route-state, and deployment-status events.
Inspect `llmRoutes`, `llmRouteStates`, and activity collections.
tests.expected_result: Bootstrap consumes relay-backed events after EOSE, valid Bahia-authored LLM events populate browser-visible collections, and live events remain reactive after bootstrap.
data_requirements: Stable Bahia service pubkey, relay URL, and LLM route/state/status event fixtures.
determinism_notes: Tests inject events directly through mocked query/subscription interfaces; no live relay is used.

tests.title: Browser control-plane store ignores spoofed non-Bahia LLM events
tests.description: Extend the store suite with an explicit spoofed-author case for LLM route/state or activity events, not just generic service registry events. Estimated implementation difficulty: low.
preconditions: The store has bootstrapped with an advertised Bahia service pubkey.
steps: Inject spoofed LLM route or route-state events from a non-Bahia pubkey.
Inject spoofed LLM deployment status/result activity from a non-Bahia pubkey.
Inspect LLM collections and activity feed.
tests.expected_result: Spoofed non-Bahia LLM events are ignored and do not mutate `llmRoutes`, `llmRouteStates`, or LLM activity state.
data_requirements: Stable non-Bahia pubkey and spoofed LLM event fixtures.
determinism_notes: Extend the existing mocked-store suite; no external services are required.

tests.title: Dedicated browser LLM workflow exercises route creation, release registration, deploy initiation, approval visibility, and relay-backed state
tests.description: Dedicated browser workflow proof for the approved user-facing contract. Implemented via a deterministic relay-backed Playwright harness and dedicated `/llm` route. Estimated implementation difficulty: high; now completed.
preconditions: The web app exposes a dedicated LLM workflow page or route.
Signer-first browser request helpers and relay-backed read models are wired for the LLM slice.
A deterministic Bahia-backed test harness is available for signed request/result flows.
steps: Open the dedicated LLM workflow in the browser.
Create an LLM route.
Register a release.
Initiate deployment and observe approval visibility and resulting route-state/activity updates.
Inspect network or harness traces to confirm signer-first request kinds and relay-backed state usage.
tests.expected_result: The browser workflow exists, is user-visible, drives signer-first LLM request kinds, and surfaces resulting route/state/activity without relying on deprecated operational REST mutation endpoints.
fixtures: Bahia e2e harness with deterministic relay fixtures
mocks: signer fixture for browser automation if required
data_requirements: Stable environment, route, release, and requester fixtures suitable for repeatable browser automation.
determinism_notes: Uses a deterministic Bahia Playwright harness that intercepts signer-first WebSocket publishes and synthesizes correlated relay-visible projections/results.
Does not rely on live external relays or model providers.
Explicitly asserts the browser workflow avoids deprecated `/api/v1/llm/**` mutation endpoints.

tests.title: Legacy operational REST mutation endpoints stay disabled by default and compatibility-only behind operator access
tests.description: Existing router tests prove the deprecated mutation routes are not mounted by default and remain compatibility-only behind explicit operator gating. Estimated implementation difficulty: none.
preconditions: Router can be constructed once with default config and once with `AllowOperationalREST=true` plus operator auth enabled.
steps: POST to deprecated operational REST mutation endpoints with default config.
Verify they return 404 by default.
Repeat intent creation with compatibility mode enabled for unauthorized, forbidden, and operator callers.
tests.expected_result: Deprecated operational REST mutations are absent by default and only reachable as an explicitly gated compatibility surface.
data_requirements: Stable test auth keys for operator and non-operator callers.
determinism_notes: Pure router contract test; no live relay or browser dependency.

known_gaps: Rollback-specific tests remain intentionally excluded because rollback acceptance criteria were deferred by HITL-LLM_ROUTE_RELEASE_DEPLOYMENT-004.

implementation_notes: `internal/controlplane/reactor_llm_requests_test.go` covers Bahia-side signed request/result correlation for route create, release register, deploy acceptance, approval, rejection, and invalid decision handling.
`internal/controlplane/llm_command_publisher_test.go` now covers canonical route-create and release-register publisher paths in addition to deploy and rollback publisher contracts.
`internal/mcp/server_llm_test.go` now proves MCP route-create and release-register tools publish canonical signer-first Nostr requests instead of mutating the registry directly.
`internal/service/llm_provisioning_coordinator_test.go` now verifies coordinator success-path progress/completion and failure-path terminal error behavior for AC-006.
`web/tests/unit/public-controlplane.test.js` adds direct browser-request helper coverage for signer-first LLM route, release, deploy, and approval requests.

`web/src/routes/llm/+page.svelte`, `web/tests/e2e/harnesses/llm-controlplane-public.js`, and `web/tests/e2e/llm-route-release-deployment.spec.js` now provide deterministic end-to-end coverage for the dedicated browser workflow required by AC-009.
`web/tests/unit/controlplane-store.test.js` includes explicit spoofed non-Bahia LLM route/state/activity regression coverage for AC-008.
